ModMetaData.name: Shift Change
ModMetaData.author: MrBeverage
ModMetaData.description:
REQUIRES ODYSSEY (for the outfit stand) AND HARMONY.
In a game with so many choices of arms, armor, and apparel, why limit yourself to just one set for all jobs? There is different gear best for work, play, combat - use all of them!
With Shift Change, colonists can change into the right clothes for the room they are going to, whether they are there to work, to enjoy themselves, or to sleep, and back out again afterwards.
Put a vanilla outfit stand in a room and put an outfit on it. Each stand dresses for one of three things.
Your doctor operates in combat armor. It's always been on, and never taken off.
Work. A colonist taking on automatic work of that room's kind (doctoring in the hospital, researching in the lab, cooking in the kitchen) changes into the stand's outfit before starting, and back when their work takes them elsewhere.
Somewhere in your stockpile is probably not a set of formal wear that nobody has ever put on. So go make some, and put them in the rec room.
Recreation. A stand set to recreation will dress anyone who arrives in that room to enjoy themselves, and change them back when they leave. A room the game already scores as a rec room switches itself on; a throne room or a pool does not, and takes the switch by hand.
Your space marine has been sleeping in their cataphract armor since the day you got it.
Sleeping. A stand in the bedroom hands out whatever is on it at bedtime and holds their day clothes until morning. A bedroom switches this on by itself. A barracks does not, and takes the switch by hand, because a stand serves one colonist at a time and the first sleeper to reach it would hold it all night. The work type called resting in bed is vanilla's medical bed rest and is a separate thing; a stand set to sleeping ignores it.
A colonist woken and drafted stays in whatever they are wearing. Undraft them and the ordinary change back happens on their next job.
Their own clothes wait in the stand in every case, and come back exactly as they were, force-worn markers included.
Rooms are read from their role, so hospitals, laboratories, kitchens, workshops, barns, rec rooms and bedrooms all work with no setup at all.
Most of this you will never touch. Five optional controls per stand, each shipping on a default that already works: - Shared (set owners) restricts a stand to the colonists you list: one for a personal kit, several to serve a group and nobody outside it. Left unassigned it is shared, like a bed, so a kitchen needs one stand per cook working at the same time, not one stand per cook. All / Men / Women tabs and an Assign all button make a stand the women's stand in two clicks, which matters for gendered clothing: a stand serves anyone who can wear something on it, so a shared stand holding a prestige robe and a ladies hat will put a man in the robe and leave the hat. - The stand's switch, labeled with what it currently dresses for, opens the checklist for rooms the game reads oddly, rooms that do two jobs, or a decorative stand you do not want used at all. It also names what the game reads the room as, which explains the surprises: a crib turns a hospital into a barracks. Work types, recreation and sleeping are mutually exclusive, so a room that does two of them wants two stands. - Change the whole outfit, off by default, is the difference between a lab coat worn over ordinary clothes and a sauna robe worn instead of them. Ticked, the colonist wears only what the stand holds, and loses whatever their own clothes were providing, warmth included. That is worth a thought before a robe rack in a cold biome. A mod setting, Keep colonists decent, is off by default; enable it and a stand will hold back their innermost garments rather than leave them without basic clothing. Nudists and nudism ideoligions are exempt from that whether it is on or not. - Deposit only, off by default and meaningful only on a sleeping stand, hands out no outfit at all. A colonist heading for bed parks whatever the stand's storage filter accepts, keeps the rest of their clothes on, and collects it in the morning. It is the setting for a rack beside the bed that a marine drops power armor onto every night. Narrow the storage filter before using it: a new stand accepts nearly all apparel, so left alone it will try to take almost everything they have on. It will never send anyone to bed naked, so a colonist wearing nothing under their armor is skipped until they have clothes underneath or something on the stand to change into. - Keep contents out of trade, on by default. Traders will otherwise buy anything sitting on an outfit stand: the uniform, and the owner's own clothes parked there while they are on shift. That is vanilla behavior, it reaches caravans at the gate and ships in orbit alike, and nothing else about the stand prevents it. Untick it for a stand you keep as a shop shelf.
The stand's Allow removing items toggle is held off while the stand is in service, because turning it on exposes the contents to every colonist's outfit optimizer, which will wear the uniform as everyday clothes if it outscores what they have on. It has never covered trade, which is why that is a separate switch. To take a garment back, use the eject button in the stand's Contents tab. To retire a stand and let haulers empty it, set it to Not used for shift changes, which frees the toggle.
The rules it follows: - Automatic only, for work, recreation and sleeping alike. A direct order is never delayed by a wardrobe trip, and a colonist already in uniform keeps it on. - Emergencies are never delayed. While the map is under threat nobody changes into a uniform, but a colonist already wearing one still changes back out of it. - Personal kit stays personal. A stand with owners serves only them, and nobody takes clothes out of a stand somebody else is using. - Passing through a room changes nothing; only doing the room's work does. - A meal break gets them out of uniform first, unless the food is already in their hands or their pack. That exception does not apply to a sleeping stand: a colonist wakes up standing beside it, so they change before going to eat either way. - If a stand frees up while someone is already working in its room out of uniform, they step over and change, unless they are mid-treatment on a patient. - A Change back button appears on any colonist currently in a uniform, for when you want them out of it now.
Four things recreation will not do: drinking and drug-taking do not count, because fetching a beer is the same job in a bar or a corridor; reading is left alone, because a colonist picks their reading spot after setting off; outdoors is excluded for now, since every outdoor cell resolves to the same map-spanning room, though a walled but roofless yard is its own room and still counts; and nobody is pulled out of bed, because vanilla gives patients recreation they can take lying down.
One setting: Unassigned stands are shared, on by default.
Adds no clothing, no buildings and no art of its own; it uses the vanilla outfit stand and whatever apparel you put on it.
Worth knowing before you build one: vanilla has no scrubs and no chef's whites, and the one lab coat it does have is Anomaly's, so there is very little to actually dress anyone in. Any apparel mod fixes that.
